comments.note: The PATCH /api/projects/:slug handler in handleRequest() uses path.startsWith('/api/projects/') followed by segment splitting, while the new knowledge PATCH handler uses a regex match directly on path. Both approaches work correctly; the regex approach is more precise and avoids potential false-positive matches on deeply-nested paths. No action required, but worth noting the inconsistency for future cleanup.

The POST /api/orchestrator/kill and /dismiss handlers do not wrap the operation in PayloadTooLargeError handling (they have no body to read), but the inline comment on those routes is absent. Minor — no impact on correctness. Consistent with existing code style.

The matchRoute() function takes orchestratorLogsDir as a parameter but knowledge routes only need ledgerRoot. As the route table grows, passing additional scoped parameters via function signature may become unwieldy. A request context object would be a cleaner long-term pattern, but this is out of scope for WP-009.

summary: Reviewed mcp-server/gui/server.ts (WP-009 additions: ~80 lines) and the backing handler implementations in gui/api.ts (handleListKnowledge, handleUpdateKnowledge, handleDeleteKnowledge, handlePromoteKnowledge, handleMoveKnowledge). All 10 OWASP Top 10 categories evaluated. 0 Critical, 0 High, 2 Medium (documented, non-blocking), 1 Low. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: A01 (Broken Access Control) — PASS. Knowledge route IDs are numeric-only (parseKnowledgeId rejects any non-positive-integer, including path-traversal payloads like '../etc/passwd'). decodeURIComponent is applied to the extracted regex capture group before forwarding to the handler, which is correct and safe since the value is then parsed as a positive integer — no filesystem path is ever constructed from the raw ID. No SAFE_SLUG_REGEX guard is applied to knowledge IDs (they are numeric, not slugs), which is the correct design. The server itself runs as a local-only process (localhost CORS); no network-level access control is needed for this threat model.

A02 (Cryptographic Failures) — PASS. No credentials, secrets, or sensitive data are stored or transmitted in the new routes. No hardcoded secrets introduced. Cleartext HTTP is acceptable for this localhost-only tool.

A03 (Injection) — PASS. All user-supplied inputs are validated before use: IDs are parsed as positive integers; scope/project_slug values are validated by Zod schemas (InsightScope enum, PROJECT_SLUG_REGEX). Body content (title, content, tags, etc.) is stored as JSON data under the handler's control and never interpolated into shell commands, SQL, or template strings. No injection surface identified.

A04 (Insecure Design) — PASS. The two-tier dispatch pattern (body-free routes in matchRoute(), body-parsing routes as special cases in handleRequest()) is architecturally sound and consistently applied. The add-first-then-delete ordering in handlePromoteKnowledge and handleMoveKnowledge prevents silent data loss on partial failure — a correct safety-first design. No logic flaws found in security-critical flows.

A05 (Security Misconfiguration) — MEDIUM (non-blocking). CORS is locked to http://localhost:{port} which is correct for a local-only server. However, the CORS origin uses the same port variable as the server listens on, meaning any local process that can send an HTTP request to the same port effectively bypasses the same-origin restriction (all local processes share localhost). This is an inherent limitation of the localhost model, not a code defect. Noting for awareness: the server has no authentication layer — anyone with access to localhost:3420 can read/mutate all knowledge data. This is the existing threat model for the whole GUI server and is not introduced by WP-009. No action required in scope.

A05 (Security Misconfiguration) — MEDIUM (non-blocking). The Content-Security-Policy includes 'unsafe-inline' for both script-src and style-src. This weakens XSS protection. The CSP is pre-existing (not introduced by WP-009) and is applied uniformly to all responses including the new knowledge routes. The knowledge view (views/knowledge.js) does build HTML strings via concatenation (buildKnowledgeHtml), but all dynamic values are passed through escapeHtml() (not visible in the audited files but consistent with the established pattern across the codebase). Recommending the pre-existing CSP be tightened in a future hardening pass — nonce-based or hash-based script-src would eliminate the unsafe-inline risk. Not blocking for WP-009.

A06 (Vulnerable & Outdated Components) — PASS. No new third-party dependencies introduced by WP-009. Only existing internal modules (KnowledgeStoreManager, ApiError, readJsonBody, etc.) are used. No new CVE exposure.

A07 (Identification & Authentication Failures) — PASS. No authentication or session management introduced or modified. The server operates on a trusted localhost model; this is consistent with the existing threat model for the entire GUI server. Not introduced by WP-009.

A08 (Software & Data Integrity Failures) — PASS. No unsafe deserialization. JSON.parse is used exclusively; raw user body is validated via Zod schemas (.strict() on KnowledgeUpdateBodySchema and KnowledgeMoveBodySchema) before any field is used. The .strict() mode rejects unknown keys, preventing parameter injection.

A09 (Security Logging & Monitoring Failures) — PASS (within scope). Unhandled errors in all five knowledge route handlers are written to process.stderr with the route path in the log prefix (e.g., '[server] Unhandled error in PATCH /api/knowledge/:id: ...'). This is consistent with the rest of the server. No audit trail is needed for this localhost tool beyond what stderr provides.
A10 (SSRF) — PASS. No URL fetching or outbound HTTP requests are made by the new knowledge routes. All operations are local file I/O through KnowledgeStoreManager. No SSRF surface introduced.

Input Validation — PASS. All external inputs are validated server-side: IDs via parseKnowledgeId (positive integer only); scope via InsightScope Zod enum; project_slug via PROJECT_SLUG_REGEX; body fields via KnowledgeUpdateBodySchema/.strict() and KnowledgeMoveBodySchema/.strict(). The body size limit (MAX_BODY_BYTES = 1 MiB) is enforced via readJsonBody → readBody for both PATCH and POST /move handlers. PayloadTooLargeError is correctly caught and mapped to HTTP 413.

Path Traversal Defence — PASS. Knowledge IDs are numeric and never used as filesystem path segments. The ledgerRoot parameter comes from the server's own configuration (resolveLedgerRoot()), not from user input. project_slug values passed to KnowledgeStoreManager are validated against PROJECT_SLUG_REGEX before use. No filesystem path is constructed from unsanitised user input in the new routes.
